solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unhappy experience of duke who makes confessions?

parts.note: one who owns up confesses, so an owner is jokingly someone who admits things

explanation.surface: A nobleman who keeps confessing has a miserable time of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who makes confessions?' reads OWNER as one who owns up; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A downer is informal for a depressing occurrence or bad time.

clue.text: Invalidate detective's rank, given fine instead of time

indicators.note: one letter stands in place of the other

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, with the possessive S
quality once meant high social rank
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A detective's promotion is cancelled, with a fine instead of a jail sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: To disqualify is to rule ineligible, making a result or claim void.

clue.text: Odd obstruction in current day

parts.note: a weir is a low dam across a river's flow

explanation.surface: A strange blockage in the stream today.
explanation.definitionFit: Weird means strange or peculiar.

clue.text: Behind Cockney Trotter's back

parts.note: the end is the rear or behind

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the aitch at the start of words

parts.note: a trotter can be a horse bred for trotting races

explanation.surface: The rear of a Cockney character named Trotter.
explanation.walkthrough: Del Boy Trotter is the Cockney hero of the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses; here a trotter is a horse, minus H the Cockney way.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to support or back a person or proposal.

clue.text: Song writer introduces taste

indicators.note: the writer comes in front of the song, leading into it in the answer

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument, so a writer
a chant is a simple sung melody

explanation.surface: A songwriter presents something to show their artistic taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song writer' looks like one person, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a liking or fondness for something, a taste for it.

clue.text: Lofty home where Providence is in view

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to eye is to view
Providence is the capital of Rhode Island, abbreviated RI

explanation.surface: A house on a height where God's care is visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Providence' looks like divine care but is the American city.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is an eagle's nest built high on a crag, so an elevated dwelling.

clue.text: Fakeish-sounding soft leather

indicators.note: the word is taken as it is pronounced

parts.note: shammy, as if sham-like, suggests something rather fake

explanation.surface: Leather that seems a bit counterfeit.
explanation.definitionFit: Chamois is supple leather from goatskin or sheepskin, used for polishing.

clue.text: Workers secured by a welcome deal

indicators.note: the workers are held inside the other pieces

parts.note: to greet is to welcome
men are workers, as in a workforce

explanation.surface: Staff are won over by a friendly reception to a pay settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: An agreement is a deal or pact.

clue.text: Thunder had a hum, initially ignored

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell, so had a hum means smelled

explanation.surface: Thunder rumbled with a drone at first unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: To tank or thunder along is to travel fast and heavily, a usage recorded in Chambers.

clue.text: Cable involving blue (Conservative) know-all

indicators.note: the cable wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a cable is a wire
the blue is the sea

explanation.surface: A telegram about a Tory politician who thinks he knows everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' suggests Conservative colours, but here it is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is a smart alec who claims to know everything.

clue.text: After a change of side, laundry appliance becomes less sturdy

indicators.note: right is swapped for left, so the R abbreviation gives way to an L

parts.note: a spin drier is a machine that spins wet washing dry

explanation.surface: A washing machine that switches sides grows wobbly.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) becomes L (left) in SPIN DRIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Spindly means thin and weak-looking, so the comparative describes something frailer.

clue.text: Answer in favour of new extension to stage

parts.note: pro means for, supporting

explanation.surface: A reply backing a proposal to build onto a theatre's stage.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre the apron is the part of the stage projecting in front of the curtain.

clue.text: What's jumping in puddle ever done? Showing immaturity

indicators.note: letters jumping about land in a new order, as a child leaping in a puddle

explanation.surface: Splashing about in puddles is the mark of a childish person.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not fully grown or matured is stunted in development, hence immature.

clue.text: Modern author to write finally among Brown and company

indicators.note: the pieces are set within the brown and company

parts.note: umber is a brown pigment

indicators.note: the final letter of the word write is taken

explanation.surface: A contemporary writer finishes his book among Dan Brown and others.
explanation.definitionFit: Umberto Eco was the Italian novelist who wrote The Name of the Rose.

clue.text: Forward movement mostly not relying on gills?

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, so its final letter is cut off

parts.note: a creature breathing with lungs rather than gills could be called lunged

explanation.surface: A fish-like creature moving forward without using gills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lunged' (having lungs) is a playful coinage; drop its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a sudden thrust or step forwards, as in fencing.

clue.text: Owner upset footless oversized countryman

indicators.note: the letters are knocked over into a new order
in a down clue the foot is the bottom letter, which is removed

parts.note: giant means very large

explanation.surface: A proprietor topples a huge legless fellow countryman.
explanation.definitionFit: A countryman here is a native of a country, a Scandinavian from Norway.

clue.text: Souls come to play here?

indicators.note: letters set to play move freely around into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A venue where spirits gather for entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: gladiators' souls came to the Roman arena to 'play', and many died there.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colosseum is Rome's great amphitheatre where gladiatorial games were staged.

clue.text: Pleasant area in one Oxford college supporting learner

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes beneath, so the learner comes first

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for learner, as on L-plates
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the college

parts.note: Keble is a college of Oxford University

explanation.surface: A nice district inside an Oxford college that helps a student.
explanation.definitionFit: Likeable means pleasant and easy to like.

clue.text: Fanatic bottling anger with Black Forest safety measure?

indicators.note: the fanatic holds the other pieces inside, as a bottle contains liquid

parts.note: a freak is an enthusiast, as in a fitness freak
ire means anger
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An enthusiast keeping a lid on dark rage before a woodland outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleared strip of land in woodland stops a wildfire spreading, a precaution against blazes.

clue.text: Anonymous old poem book lifted illness misery

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces are raised, so they read upwards

parts.note: flu is an illness
woe is misery

explanation.surface: A book relieved the misery of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Beowulf is the Old English epic poem whose author is unknown.

clue.text: Improper way to have head deferred

indicators.note: the leading letter is put off until later, moving to the end

parts.note: a route is a way to go

explanation.surface: It is wrong to put off dealing with your boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré describes something unconventional or beyond the bounds of propriety.

clue.text: Monster demanding source of windfalls?

parts.note: an orc is a monster of fantasy fiction
hard means difficult or demanding

explanation.surface: A greedy monster after a lucky payout.
explanation.walkthrough: Windfalls look like money gains but are fruit blown from trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit trees in a plantation shed apples blown down by the wind.

clue.text: Film story which hopes to increase funds?

parts.note: a film is a thin layer, a deposit of sediment
an account is a narrative or story

explanation.surface: A movie plot about raising money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' suggests a movie, but here it is a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A savings arrangement at a bank paying interest is held in the hope the money grows.

clue.text: Frame taken from Monmouthshire village to Bury

indicators.note: the outer letters, which frame the word, are removed

parts.note: Tintern is a village in Monmouthshire, Wales, known for its abbey

explanation.surface: Travelling from a Welsh village to the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town near Manchester, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to place a body in a grave.

clue.text: University do a number on drugs

parts.note: to perform a number is to sing a song

explanation.surface: A student performance under the influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone taking narcotics habitually is described as a user, currently consuming them.

clue.text: Don't talk work, which talking this is

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Advice not to discuss your job.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes a phrase: talking about one's work is 'talking ____'.
explanation.definitionFit: A store where work is talked about gives the idiom for discussing one's job socially.

clue.text: Announcement of top-level takeover in three lines

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken, so the words are taken as heard

parts.note: a high coup is a seizure of power at the very top

explanation.surface: A short notice about a boardroom takeover written in brief form.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a Japanese verse form of three lines totalling seventeen syllables.

clue.text: Strained at, like vat full of gas?

indicators.note: the letters are forced out of shape into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Wine filtered through a vat bubbling with gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full of gas' sounds chemical but means chatty.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone full of gas, or hot air, chatters at length.

clue.text: 11 turned in engineer of an iPad

indicators.note: the concealed letters are read from right to left
the letters sit inside the run of words engineer of an iPad

explanation.surface: An engineer's tablet gets folded over.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' refers to the answer at 11 across, a garment worn over clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is a sleeveless garment worn over clothes, a kind of apron.

clue.text: Slowly, an enlisted man gets into trouble

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the word for trouble

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble
a GI is an American enlisted soldier

explanation.surface: A recruit sinks gradually into difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical direction for playing at a slow tempo.
